title: "GEN242: Data Analysis in Genome Biology"
subtitle: "Graduate course materials by Thomas Girke — University of California, Riverside"
page-layout: full
toc: false
---

This course introduces computational approaches for working with genome-scale
data. It covers core concepts, algorithms, data analysis workflows, and
programming skills used in modern genome biology. Students gain practical
experience with R, reproducible research, NGS analysis, and interpretation of
genomics results.

## Course components

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-6 .g-col-md-4}
### [Slides](slides/index.qmd)
Lecture slide decks organized by topic. Topics include foundations in genome biology,
Linux/HPC, Git/GitHub, R programming, reproducible reporting, basic statistical
methods, NGS algorithms and analysis workflows, functional enrichment
analysis, clustering, and ML/AI for genomics.
:::

::: {.g-col-6 .g-col-md-4}
### [Tutorials](tutorials/index.qmd)
Step-by-step computational tutorials introducing the basics of working on
Linux/HPC systems and data analysis programming in R. Tutorial topics are
connected to a wide range of analysis areas related to the course projects.
:::

::: {.g-col-6 .g-col-md-4}
### [Assignments](assignments/index.qmd)
Homework assignments and a course project covering key analysis topics in
genome biology. Project topics change each year based on students' interests.
Recent topics have included bulk and single-cell NGS analysis, functional
interpretation, AI/ML methods, and multi-omics data integration.
:::

:::
